content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I need a box, that is on the upside open. The outer dimensions are 220 x 300 x 160mm. The wall thickness should be 8mm and the bottom thickness 12mm | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Implementation concept – step by step (no function calls executed yet)

1. Establish the coordinate system  
   • Origin (0 , 0 , 0) will be taken as the lower-front-left corner of the box.  
   • +X points to the right, +Y points to the back, +Z points upward.

2. Create the outer shell (solid starting volume)  
   • One rectangular block is added with the exact outside dimensions the user gave:  
     – X-size = 220 mm, Y-size = 300 mm, Z-size = 160 mm.  
   • Basepoint (x, y, z) = (0 , 0 , 0).  
   • Because this is the very first solid, the parameter subtraction is False.

3. Carve out the open interior (subtract the cavity)  
   • The cavity’s sizes are obtained by removing twice the wall thickness from X and Y, and removing only the bottom thickness from Z:  
     – X-size   = 220 – 2 · 8  = 204 mm  
     – Y-size   = 300 – 2 · 8  = 284 mm  
     – Z-size   = 160 – 12     = 148 mm (so the top stays open and 12 mm bottom remains)  
   • The cavity must start 8 mm inwards from both X and Y directions and 12 mm above the bottom plane, therefore the block’s basepoint is (8 , 8 , 12).  
   • This block is marked with subtraction = True so it is removed from the outer solid.

4. Finalize  
   • After the two block operations, the finished() function will be issued with allFunctionsCalled = True to indicate the model is complete.

These two block calls (outer shell add, inner cavity subtract) are the only geometry-producing steps needed; no cylinders or other operations are required.  

When you say “prepare the function call,” I will provide the exact JSON payloads for block() and finished() in the required order, ready to be run.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
